sequences.title: VK-only Read Coils: The report describes a heap-based buffer overflow in `read_io_status` in `src/modbus.c`. It was observed when the `tests/unit-test-client` utility executed `modbus_read_bits(ctx, UT_BITS_ADDRESS, UT_BITS_NB + 1, tab_rp_bits)` at `tests/unit-test-client.c:363` and received a mutated Read Coils response. The normal response `001100000006ff0101300026` was changed by modifying the Modbus ADU `unitId` from `0xff` to `0x7c`, producing `0011000000067c0101300023`. Under AddressSanitizer, this caused a size-1 heap write in `read_io_status` at `src/modbus.c:1207`, reached from `modbus_read_bits`, and the client crashed with a reported `heap-buffer-overflow`.

sequences.title: VK-only Read Discrete Inputs: In libmodbus-3.1.10, an intermittent crash is reported in `read_registers()` in `modbus.c` at line 1313, reached from `modbus_read_input_registers(ctx, 0, 7, reg)`. The failing statement is the loop that stores response data into `dest[i]`; the provided backtrace shows `dest=0x1` and inaccessible at that point. The report does not identify the root cause or a specific missing validation, although the reporter states the original `reg` array address looked valid in gdb. The documented trigger is reading 7 input registers starting at address 0 from the device, and the demonstrated impact is an intermittent process crash.

The sample input provided is <00><01><02><00><80><04><01><01><2A>. The report says this produces undefined behavior and crashes, with ASan indicating a heap-buffer-overflow; the mention of other unintended behaviors is speculative.
